extracted.intended_audience: clinical trial investigators, sponsors, trial methodologists, IRBs/RECs, funders, journal editors, and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for the minimum content to include in a clinical trial protocol (SPIRIT 2013), specifying 33 core protocol items and related registry data elements to ensure transparency, replicability, and ethical/scientific appraisal. Applicable primarily to randomized trials but relevant to all clinical trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title (Item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptive title identifying the study design, population, interventions, and, if applicable, trial acronym
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title should clearly identify design, population, and interventions so protocol users and readers can immediately understand the trial scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial registration (Item 2a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial identifier and registry name. If not yet registered, name of intended registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide registry identifier and name; if not registered, state intended registry to promote prospective registration and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial registration data set (Item 2b)
rubrics_metrics.description: All items from the World Health Organization Trial Registration Data Set (Appendix Table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPIRIT recommends listing the WHO Trial Registration Data Set in the protocol (see Appendix Table). Having this data set in the protocol helps create complete registry entries and facilitates updates when amendments occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol version (Item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Date and version identifier
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocols must include dated version identifiers; amendments should be tracked and dated to provide a transparent audit trail of changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding (Item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources and types of financial, material, and other support
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose all sources and types of funding/support to allow assessment of potential influences on trial design, conduct, and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities — protocol contributors (Item 5a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names, affiliations, and roles of protocol contributors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List individuals who contributed to protocol development with affiliations and specific roles to document contributors and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities — sponsor contact (Item 5b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Name and contact information for the trial sponsor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear sponsor contact details for accountability and queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities — sponsor/funder role (Item 5c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of study sponsor and funders, if any, in study design; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of data; writing of the report; and the decision to submit the report for publication, including whether they will have ultimate authority over any of these activities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly disclose sponsor/funder involvement in core trial activities and any ultimate authority to allow assessment of independence and potential conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities — oversight composition (Item 5d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition, roles, and responsibilities of the coordinating center, steering committee, end point adjudication committee, data management team, and other individuals or groups overseeing the trial, if applicable (see item 21a for DMC)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe oversight structures, their composition, and responsibilities so readers can understand governance and decision-making processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and rationale (Item 6a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of research question and justification for undertaking the trial, including summary of relevant studies (published and unpublished) examining benefits and harms for each intervention
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear rationale with an evidence summary that situates the trial question within existing knowledge, including harms and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and rationale — choice of comparators (Item 6b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation for choice of comparators
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify comparator selection (e.g., placebo, usual care, active control) so results are interpretable relative to alternative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (Item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific objectives or hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State primary and secondary objectives/hypotheses explicitly to align design, outcomes, and analyses with stated aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial design (Item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of trial design, including type of trial (e.g., parallel group, crossover, factorial, single group), allocation ratio, and framework (e.g., superiority, equivalence, noninferiority, exploratory)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe overall design features and trial framework so statistical and methodological choices can be understood and judged appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study setting (Item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of study settings (e.g., community clinic, academic hospital) and list of countries where data will be collected. Reference to where list of study sites can be obtained
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify settings and countries to clarify external validity and provide or reference site lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria (Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion and exclusion criteria for participants. If applicable, eligibility criteria for study centers and individuals who will perform the interventions (e.g., surgeons, psychotherapists)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear participant, center, and provider eligibility criteria to enable replication and assessment of applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions — description (Item 11a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interventions for each group with sufficient detail to allow replication, including how and when they will be administered
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe interventions comprehensively (dosage, timing, procedures, materials) so others with appropriate expertise can replicate them; include training materials and figures if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions — discontinuation/modification criteria (Item 11b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for discontinuing or modifying allocated interventions for a given trial participant (e.g., drug dose change in response to harms, participant request, or improving/worsening disease)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State pre-specified rules for intervention modification or discontinuation to ensure consistent handling of participant safety and protocol deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions — adherence strategies (Item 11c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies to improve adherence to intervention protocols, and any procedures for monitoring adherence (e.g., drug tablet return, laboratory tests)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline adherence-enhancing strategies and monitoring methods to minimize differential adherence and to document compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions — concomitant care (Item 11d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant concomitant care and interventions that are permitted or prohibited during the trial
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe allowed/prohibited co-interventions to avoid contamination and clarify comparability between groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes (Item 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary, secondary, and other outcomes, including the specific measurement variable (e.g., systolic blood pressure), analysis metric (e.g., change from baseline, final value, time to event), method of aggregation (e.g., median, proportion), and time point for each outcome. Explanation of the clinical relevance of chosen efficacy and harm outcomes is strongly recommended
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define outcomes precisely (variable, metric, aggregation, time point) and explain clinical relevance; link primary outcome to sample size calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant timeline (Item 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time schedule of enrollment, interventions (including any run-ins and washouts), assessments, and visits for participants. A schematic diagram is highly recommended (Figure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear timeline and consider including a schematic schedule to aid comprehension of trial flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size (Item 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated number of participants needed to achieve study objectives and how it was determined, including clinical and statistical assumptions supporting any sample size calculations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give sample size estimate with underlying assumptions and calculations to allow appraisal of power and precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment (Item 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies for achieving adequate participant enrollment to reach target sample size
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe recruitment approaches and contingencies to demonstrate feasibility of achieving planned sample size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation sequence generation (Item 16a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method of generating the allocation sequence (e.g., computer-generated random numbers), and list of any factors for stratification. To reduce predictability of a random sequence, details of any planned restriction (e.g., blocking) should be provided in a separate document that is unavailable to those who enroll participants or assign interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe sequence generation, stratification factors, and note that detailed restriction methods (e.g., block sizes) should be kept separate to maintain concealment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation concealment mechanism (Item 16b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanism of implementing the allocation sequence (e.g., central telephone; sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes), describing any steps to conceal the sequence until interventions are assigned
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain practical steps ensuring allocation concealment to prevent selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation (Item 16c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who will generate the allocation sequence, who will enroll participants, and who will assign participants to interventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State roles and separation of duties to ensure integrity of sequence generation, enrollment, and assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding (masking) — who blinded (Item 17a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who will be blinded after assignment to interventions (e.g., trial participants, care providers, outcome assessors, data analysts), and how
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which parties are blinded and describe methods to maintain blinding where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding — unblinding procedures (Item 17b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If blinded, circumstances under which unblinding is permissible, and procedure for revealing a participant’s allocated intervention during the trial
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define explicit unblinding criteria and procedures to handle emergencies or other justified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection methods — assessment and instruments (Item 18a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for assessment and collection of outcome, baseline, and other trial data, including any related processes to promote data quality (e.g., duplicate measurements, training of assessors) and a description of study instruments (e.g., questionnaires, laboratory tests) along with their reliability and validity, if known. Reference to where data collection forms can be found, if not in the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe measurement methods, quality assurance procedures, and psychometric properties or validation of instruments; reference data collection forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection methods — retention and follow-up (Item 18b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans to promote participant retention and complete follow-up, including list of any outcome data to be collected for participants who discontinue or deviate from intervention protocols
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify retention strategies and the data to be collected from participants who discontinue to allow intention-to-treat and sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management (Item 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for data entry, coding, security, and storage, including any related processes to promote data quality (e.g., double data entry; range checks for data values). Reference to where details of data management procedures can be found, if not in the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe data handling procedures, quality checks, and security measures; reference detailed data management plans if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods — primary/secondary analyses (Item 20a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical methods for analyzing primary and secondary outcomes. Reference to where other details of the statistical analysis plan can be found, if not in the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide main statistical approaches and reference the full statistical analysis plan to ensure reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods — additional analyses (Item 20b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for any additional analyses (e.g., subgroup and adjusted analyses)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify subgroup, adjusted, and exploratory analyses and their rationale to reduce risk of data-driven reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods — analysis population and missing data (Item 20c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of analysis population relating to protocol nonadherence (e.g., as-randomized analysis), and any statistical methods to handle missing data (e.g., multiple imputation)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define primary analysis population (e.g., intent-to-treat) and missing-data strategies to allow interpretation of robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data monitoring — composition and role of DMC (Item 21a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of DMC; summary of its role and reporting structure; statement of whether it is independent from the sponsor and competing interests; and reference to where further details about its charter can be found, if not in the protocol. Alternatively, an explanation of why a DMC is not needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe DMC membership, independence, role, and reporting lines; if no DMC, justify the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data monitoring — interim analyses and stopping guidelines (Item 21b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of any interim analyses and stopping guidelines, including who will have access to these interim results and make the final decision to terminate the trial
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify interim analysis plans, stopping boundaries, and decision-making processes to prevent ad hoc stopping and bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harms (Item 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for collecting, assessing, reporting, and managing solicited and spontaneously reported adverse events and other unintended effects of trial interventions or trial conduct
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail adverse event collection, grading, reporting timelines, and management to ensure participant safety and transparent reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditing (Item 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency and procedures for auditing trial conduct, if any, and whether the process will be independent from investigators and the sponsor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State audit plans and independence to support regulatory compliance and quality assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research ethics approval (Item 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for seeking REC/IRB approval
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe ethics approval plans, including where applications will be submitted and documentation to be retained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol amendments (Item 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for communicating important protocol modifications (e.g., changes to eligibility criteria, outcomes, analyses) to relevant parties (e.g., investigators, RECs/IRBs, trial participants, trial registries, journals, regulators)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify mechanisms and timelines for amendment communication and updating trial registries and participant information as needed; maintain transparent audit trail with dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent or assent — obtaining consent (Item 26a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who will obtain informed consent or assent from potential trial participants or authorized surrogates, and how (see item 32)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe consent process, personnel, and documentation procedures to ensure informed and voluntary participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent — additional provisions for ancillary studies (Item 26b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional consent provisions for collection and use of participant data and biological specimens in ancillary studies, if applicable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address secondary use consent and specimen storage/analysis to respect participant autonomy and future research use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality (Item 27)
rubrics_metrics.description: How personal information about potential and enrolled participants will be collected, shared, and maintained in order to protect confidentiality before, during, and after the trial
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe data protection, de-identification, access controls, and data-sharing policies respecting confidentiality across the trial lifecycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests (Item 28)
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial and other competing interests for principal investigators for the overall trial and each study site
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require disclosure of competing interests at investigator and site levels to allow assessment of potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to data (Item 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of who will have access to the final trial data set, and disclosure of contractual agreements that limit such access for investigators
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify data access rights and any contractual limitations to support transparency and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary and post-trial care (Item 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions, if any, for ancillary and post-trial care, and for compensation to those who suffer harm from trial participation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans for post-trial care and compensation arrangements for harm to address ethical responsibilities to participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination policy — communication plans (Item 31a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for investigators and sponsor to communicate trial results to participants, health care professionals, the public, and other relevant groups (e.g., via publication, reporting in results databases, or other data-sharing arrangements), including any publication restrictions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify plans for dissemination and any restrictions to promote timely and comprehensive reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination policy — authorship (Item 31b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorship eligibility guidelines and any intended use of professional writers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define authorship criteria and declare use of professional writers to ensure transparency about writing and credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination policy — data/protocol/code access (Item 31c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans, if any, for granting public access to the full protocol, participant-level data set, and statistical code
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State intentions for sharing protocols, datasets, and code to facilitate independent verification and secondary analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent materials (Appendix Item 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model consent form and other related documentation given to participants and authorized surrogates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sample consent forms or reference them to ensure consistency with described consent procedures (see Item 26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological specimens (Appendix Item 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for collection, laboratory evaluation, and storage of biological specimens for genetic or molecular analysis in the current trial and for future use in ancillary studies, if applicable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specimen handling, storage, future use, and consent/ethics considerations for biobanking and ancillary research.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Primary registry and trial-identifying number (WHO item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of primary registry and the unique identifier assigned by the primary registry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include primary registry name and unique identifier to support tracing of registered trial record.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Date of registration (WHO item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Date when the trial was officially registered in the primary registry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record registration date; prospective registration (before first participant enrolled) is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Secondary identifying numbers (WHO item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other identifiers, if any; Universal Trial Number; identifiers assigned by the sponsor; other trial registration numbers issued by other registries; identifiers issued by funding bodies, collaborative research groups, regulatory authorities, ethics committees/institutional review boards, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List any additional identifiers to facilitate cross-referencing across systems and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Sources of monetary or material support (WHO item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Major sources of monetary or material support for the trial (e.g., funding agency, foundation, company, institution)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose principal funding/support sources for the registry record and protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Primary sponsor (WHO item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Person, organization, group, or other legal entity that takes responsibility for initiating and managing a study
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the legal sponsor responsible for trial initiation and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Secondary sponsor(s) (WHO item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional persons, organizations, or other legal persons, if any, who have agreed with the primary sponsor to take on responsibilities of sponsorship
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List secondary sponsors and their roles if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Contact for public queries (WHO item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: E-mail address, telephone number, and postal address of the contact who will respond to general queries, including information about current recruitment status
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear public contact for inquiries about recruitment and general trial information.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Contact for scientific queries (WHO item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Name and title, e-mail address, telephone number, postal address, and affiliation of the principal investigator and e-mail address, telephone number, postal address, and affiliation of the contact for scientific queries about the trial (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide scientific contacts for protocol- or methods-related questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Public title (WHO item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title intended for the lay public in easily understood language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a public-facing title to aid understanding by non-specialists and participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Scientific title (WHO item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific title of the study as it appears in the protocol submitted for funding and ethical review; include trial acronym, if available
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the formal scientific title consistent with protocol documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Countries of recruitment (WHO item 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries from which participants will be recruited
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List recruitment countries to inform on generalizability and regulatory contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Health condition(s) studied (WHO item 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary health condition(s) or problem(s) studied (e.g., depression, breast cancer, medication error)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the health condition(s) targeted to categorize the trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Intervention(s) (WHO item 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each group of the trial, record a brief intervention name plus an intervention description. For drugs, use the generic name; for other types of interventions, provide a brief descriptive name. Intervention description: Must be sufficiently detailed for it to be possible to distinguish between the groups of a study; for example, interventions involving drugs may include dosage form, dosage, frequency, and duration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise but distinguishing intervention descriptions suitable for registry entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Key inclusion and exclusion criteria (WHO item 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion and exclusion criteria for participant selection, including age and sex
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize key eligibility criteria for registry completeness and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Study type (WHO item 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method of allocation (randomized/nonrandomized); blinding/masking (identify who is blinded); assignment (e.g., single group, parallel, crossover, factorial); purpose; phase (if applicable). For randomized trials: Method of sequence generation and allocation concealment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize study design features for registry users and to meet registry/minimum reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Date of first enrollment (WHO item 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated or actual date of enrollment of the first participant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State anticipated/actual start date; registries often require this for timeliness of records.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Target sample size (WHO item 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of participants to enroll
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List target enrollment to provide scope of trial and denominator for planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Recruitment status (WHO item 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending: Participants are not yet being recruited or enrolled at any site; Recruiting; Suspended: Temporary halt in recruitment and enrollment; Complete: Participants are no longer being recruited or enrolled; Other
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify current recruitment status to inform on trial progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Primary outcome(s) (WHO item 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary outcome should be the outcome used in sample size calculations or the main outcome used to determine the effects of the intervention. For each primary outcome provide: Name of the outcome (do not use abbreviations); Metric or method of measurement used (be as specific as possible); Time point of primary interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure primary outcome is clearly defined, matches sample size basis, and is described unambiguously in registry and protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO Trial Registration Data Set — Key secondary outcome(s) (WHO item 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: As for primary outcomes, for each secondary outcome provide: Name of the outcome (do not use abbreviations); Metric or method of measurement used (be as specific as possible); Time point of interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define secondary outcomes with the same level of specificity as primary outcomes for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Clinical Trial Protocol (general standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol defined as a document that provides sufficient detail to enable understanding of the background, rationale, objectives, study population, interventions, methods, statistical analyses, ethical considerations, dissemination plans, and administration of the trial; replication of key aspects of trial methods and conduct; and appraisal of the trial’s scientific and ethical rigor from ethics approval to dissemination of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol should be cohesive, provide appropriate context and narrative (not just a list of items), and include materials (e.g., training materials, figures) needed to enable replication by those with appropriate expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol as a living document and amendment tracking (general standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The protocol is a 'living' document that is often modified during the trial. A transparent audit trail with dates of important changes in trial design and conduct is an essential part of the scientific record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and date amendments; report important amendments to IRBs, registries, and in trial reports to maintain transparency and enable assessment of selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol content vs. format and recommended formatting conventions (general guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: SPIRIT primarily relates to content rather than format, but adherence to certain formatting conventions, such as a table of contents; section headings; glossary; list of abbreviations; list of references; and a schematic schedule of enrollment, interventions, and assessments, will facilitate protocol review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear formatting to facilitate review and usability; content should still be the primary focus but good format improves efficiency of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing related documents rather than duplicating (general guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant details may appear in related documents, such as statistical analysis plans, case record forms, operations manuals, or investigator contracts. In these instances, the protocol should outline the key principles and refer to the separate documents so that their existence is known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize key principles in protocol and reference supporting documents; ensure referenced documents are identifiable and accessible where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SPIRIT with Explanation and Elaboration (recommended practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is strongly recommended that this checklist be read in conjunction with the SPIRIT 2013 Explanation and Elaboration for important clarification on the items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Explanation & Elaboration paper for rationale, supporting evidence, model examples, and further guidance on addressing each checklist item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended use and limits of SPIRIT (interpretive standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent of SPIRIT 2013 is to promote transparency and a full description of what is planned — not to prescribe how a trial should be designed or conducted. The checklist should not be used to judge trial quality, because the protocol of a poorly designed trial may address all checklist items by fully describing its inadequate design features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SPIRIT to improve protocol completeness and transparency; do not conflate completeness of reporting with appropriateness of design. Use protocols for appraisal of adherence and selective reporting comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with other guidance and standards (contextual standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: SPIRIT 2013 mirrors applicable items from CONSORT 2010 and supports WHO, ICMJE, ClinicalTrials.gov, European Commission, and ICH Good Clinical Practice items, providing consistent wording to facilitate transition from protocol to final report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure protocol content aligns with registry, reporting, and regulatory expectations; consistent wording aids linkage between protocol, registry entry, and final publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder endorsement and implementation (policy/implementation standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: SPIRIT 2013 should be adopted as standard guidance by clinical trial groups, investigators, sponsors, RECs/IRBs, funding agencies, trial registries, educators, journal editors, and publishers to improve protocol quality, completeness, and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders are encouraged to endorse and implement SPIRIT, require adherence in submissions, and provide resources and training to facilitate uptake.
